decisions.reason: DNA structure and information-storage structure/function is one assessable modelling competence. Removing the distinct replication routine is warranted; DE/EN agree.

decisions.reason: Distinguishing DNA mutation types and justifying context-dependent protein consequences is one mutation-analysis competence; the revision removes the false inference that every insertion/deletion/duplication inevitably frameshifts or has the same protein effect. DE/EN agree.
decisions.sourceBoundary: HE p38 explicitly lists all four gene-mutation categories; protein-consequence reasoning is a justified authored application in the Q1 material/gen-product context. BY B12 GA/EA 2.4 supports mutation/protein-function analysis but its whole competency also involves mutagens and protective awareness: partial only. NI explicitly excludes molecular analysis. MV/RP/SH/SN/ST/TH supplied sources support various broad mutation contexts, not an exact common four-category molecular/protein scope across all six.
requiredActions: Remove unsupported NI ffef source/target bindings only together with demonstrated nonmolecular mutation/recombination coverage and usable prerequisites.

For MV/RP/SH/SN/ST/TH record separate partial/scope decisions: RP minimizes molecular details; SH variation source does not require four sequence categories; SN lists gene/chromosome/genome mutations; ST lists point/genome mutations; TH has broad types, causes/consequences; MV names mutagens and somatic/germline effects. Do not infer exact support for this whole atom from those broad points.
BY missing mutagen/protein-function/protection coverage remains open, not approved by a partial rebind.

niPreservationAudit.finding: Actual retained official NI p89 prohibits molecular mutation analysis in Sek I; p87-88 likewise postpone DNA structure/replication/protein-biosynthesis molecular aspects to Sek II. Omitted restriction in extraction is real. Existing9f wording incorrectly presents selection as a cause creating variation and requires molecularffef.
niPreservationAudit.proposed9fCorrection: Conceptually sound: mutation/recombination generate variation, selection acts on it. It needs a separately reviewed nonmolecular scope and age-fit prerequisite route; no extra goal closure.
niPreservationAudit.phenomenologicalAlternative: A narrow descriptive mutation-versus-recombination comparison is a valid candidate preservation route for class10. It does not by itself cover the earlier class6 undirected variation clause or class10 selection interplay. Separate source-component coverage remains necessary.
